newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Mestrallet sees only five core holdings for Suez.
newsitem.headline: Mestrallet sees only five core holdings for Suez.

text.p: Gerard Mestrallet, chief executive officer of Compagnie de Suez, said in a newspaper interview on Thursday that his group has five core holdings which will never be sold.
"Suez has only five participations which will never be sold," Mestrallet told Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd.
He said these were Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA, French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux, Belgian Generale Bank, French Banque Sofinco and Belgian bancassurance group Fortis AG.

"This does not mean that, for instance, (Belgian non-ferrous metals group) Union Miniere or (Belgian polyurethane sold, but unlike the five stakes mentioned earlier, these stakes are no longer essential ('incontournable')," Mestrallet said.
Suez' Belgian holdings are controlled via its 62.6 percent owned unit Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB).
SGB has built up a large debt position following a 49 billion Belgian franc acquisition of a 24.47 percent stake in Tractebel from Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL).
"A 32 billion franc debt is too high," Mestrallet said. The Suez group would have to continue its restructuring.
Mestrallet told the paper that French hotel group Accor -- of which SGB holds nine percent -- was not a strategic holding for the Suez group.
The paper estimated that an Accor sale could raise 12 billion Belgian francs for SGB. The sale of SGB's 15 percent in Luxembourg steel maker Arbed SA could raise about four billion francs, it added.
SGB has been trying to reduce its Arbed stake for several years.
